item.title: The Sales Funnel as an Algorithm
item.lead: In the dossier, the sales funnel increasingly becomes less a document and more an algorithmic control system.

blocks.text: The source describes fixed phases of recognition, vulnerability, urgency, and retention. When such phases are converted into software logic, the system can determine what type of message should follow after which event. A response, a payment moment, or a change in activity can then form a trigger.

The technical value of such a model is simple: standardize, measure, test, and optimize. The dossier then draws an ethical conclusion: when the variable in the system is not product interest but human vulnerability, optimization can escalate to behavioral manipulation.

An important concept in the source is the variable-reward funnel. Warm attention is alternated with distance or delay, causing the user, according to the hypothesis, to keep waiting for the next moment of reward. The source compares this to other systems of intermittent reinforcement. In this PDF, this is presented solely as a source hypothesis; no independent neurobiological validation has been added to it.
For technical auditing, this means that not only the output must be examined. Triggers, business rules, prompt templates, experiments, dashboards, and KPIs are also relevant sources of evidence.
